title: 1955 AHSME Problem 40
statement: If \(b\ne d,\) the fractions \(\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+d}\) and \(\dfrac bd\) are unequal if:

solutions.text:
Where the fractions are defined, equality would require \[ d(ax+b)=b(cx+d), \] which simplifies to \(x(ad-bc)=0.\) Under choice A, \(a=c=1\) gives \(ad-bc=d-b\ne0,\) and \(x\ne0,\) so equality is impossible. Each of B through E instead forces equality directly.

Thus, the fractions are unequal under choice A.
hints: After cancellation, equality is governed by \(x(ad-bc)=0\)
